name: pi-starline
notes:
Local divergence, reconstructed 2026-09-19 from diff vs upstream e54af55 (v0.3.5): (1) mouse features no longer patch TuiAltScreen.prototype — they register with the local @xzzpig/pi-mouse-events extension (optional peer >=0.1.0 <2, devDep workspace:*): wheel/press/copy handler slots, keyboard range-delete via ctx.ui.onTerminalInput; without it mouse features are simply off (no fallback), one console note per process. Click-to-expand toggles from any row of an expandable component (hint row or the component's expanded/_expanded state field), plain same-cell click only, double-click debounced; mouse/capabilities.ts probes the receiver for calling (not patching) plus copySlot; prototype-patch-registry drops the four mouse adapter keys. mouse/api-consumer.ts reads the API off Symbol.for('pi-mouse-events.api.v1') (duplicated key pinned by test/contract/mouse-api.test.ts); test/mouse/shim.ts replays the dispatch for the behavioural suites. (2) every git probe in extensions/starline/git.ts passes --no-optional-locks (index.lock churn; test/git-no-optional-locks.test.ts). (3) npm renamed @xzzpig/pi-starline, fork version 0.4.0 (0.x fork convention: upstream minor bump -> fork minor bump), README install section updated, CHANGELOG rewritten fork-only. (4) test/runtime.test.ts passes an explicit empty env to detectRuntime so ambient Nix markers (IN_NIX_SHELL) do not shadow file-marker fixtures (uses upstream's optional env param; runtime.ts itself unchanged). (5) comment-only additions: ui.ts SAFETY/pi-lens-ignore notes, config.ts empty-catch note. Keep package-lock.json in npm's native tab indentation (restored to upstream bytes + name/version lines on 2026-09-19); biome protects package-lock.json and root prettier ignores this package. Re-apply all of the above on each future sync. 2026-09-19 hardening: mouse/api-consumer.ts rejects an API object whose version !== 1, and test/contract/mouse-api.test.ts pins the slot-dispatch semantics (priority order, consume-on-first-handled, skip-throwing, fall-through) against the real implementation via the new @xzzpig/pi-mouse-events/test-support export (pi-mouse-events 0.1.2), so shim drift goes red in the contract suite. 2026-09-20 publish-gate fix: "biome check ." (prepublishOnly -> verify) failed with 3 errors, blocking the 0.4.1 publish: package.json had been re-serialized with 2-space indent by the conflict-surface refactor (upstream and biome both use TABS), and fork-only test/contract/mouse-api.test.ts was unformatted with unsorted type imports. Both fixed with "biome check --write"; no behavior change. KEEP package.json TAB-indented whenever re-applying fork name/version/deps lines after a sync, or prepublishOnly blocks the release again. editor-wheel.test.ts (upstream file) keeps 9 lint/style/noNonNullAssertion warnings and shim.ts keeps 2 lint/suspicious/noConfusingVoidType warnings by deliberate non-change: warnings do not fail biome check, and fixing them would add fork edits inside upstream files.
 2026-09-25 sync v0.3.5 -> v0.3.7 (fork 0.4.1 -> 0.5.0): merged upstream v0.3.6 (user-message markdown-transformers fix) and v0.3.7 (drop clickToExpandTools). Fork keeps the click-any-collapsible engine per design D7, so these upstream deletions were resolved as KEEP fork versions (recurring modify/delete conflicts on every future pull): extensions/starline/mouse/tool-box.ts, mouse/component-tree.ts, test/contract/tool-box-hint.test.ts, test/mouse/tool-box.test.ts, test/mouse/component-tree.test.ts, test/contract/transcript-layout.test.ts. mouse/index.ts stays the fork's 941-line consumer-API rewrite (took OURS wholesale). clickToExpandTools is NOT restored anywhere: the config key was renamed to clickToToggleExpandable (default true) at all 5 config.ts sites (MouseConfig field, FIXED_EDITOR_KEY_MAP entry clickToExpandTools->clickToToggleExpandable for fixedEditor-era migration, defaultConfig.mouse true, normalizeMouseConfig new-key-read-plus-old-key-fallback coercion, saveMousePatch spread), capabilities.ts MouseFeature union + REQUIREMENTS, mouse/index.ts feature gate, and the 7 test files; the /starline settings toggle was re-added under the new key name. handlesMouse() bow-out predicate (onMouse duck-type) was DELETED as dead code — starline owns tool rows via ToolExecutionComponent ancestor resolution; onMouse now has zero residue under mouse/. mouse/hit-test.ts was restored to fork HEAD wholesale because upstream removed scrollContentOrigin that fork tool-box.ts still imports/calls (upstream's component-tree.ts-deleted comment would lie about the fork). key-text.ts dedup: adopted upstream caa1acd3a's key-text.ts byte-stable as single source; removed the duplicate keyTextFor/fallbackKeyText from tool-box.ts; tool-box.ts and index.ts now import keyTextFor from './key-text'. capabilities.ts D8 type tightening applied: isCallable/probeCapabilities use <T extends object> (rejecting Record<string, unknown> which fails TS2345 at mouse/index.ts:238). package-lock.json kept at upstream-bytes + name/version patch (TAB indent, biome-formatted; pnpm monorepo does not consume it); package.json name @xzzpig/pi-starline version 0.5.0 with peer ranges >=0.86.0 <0.88 and devDeps ^0.87.1. pi-mouse-events 0.2.0 and pi-thinking-collapse 0.2.0 share the same >=0.86.0 <0.88 peer floor (pi 0.86.0 is when core's five MouseRegion wrappers — thinking, tool result, branch/compaction summary, skill invocation — are all native). Re-apply all of the above on each future sync; expect modify/delete conflicts on the six kept files every pull. 2026-09-25 contract v2: Starline's mouse/api-consumer.ts now reads Symbol.for('pi-mouse-events.api.v2') and rejects any candidate whose version !== 2 (pi-mouse-events 0.2.0 removed the component-dispatch half and reshaped the API, so the key and version were bumped together per api.ts's no-removal-within-a-major promise). An older published pi-mouse-events (v1) is therefore rejected, not misread: Starline's mouse features switch off with the usual console note. test/contract/mouse-api.test.ts pins the key and keeps a version:1 fixture asserting the rejection.
